finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Non‑atomic coupon decrement and multi-step order updates
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: The code reads coupon via prisma.coupon.findUnique then separately updates quantity, and the existing-order branch runs multiple sequential prisma.update/create/delete calls per item without wrapping them in a transaction. These are separate round-trips and not conditional/atomic.  
Impact: Concurrent checkouts will overspend limited coupons and produce partial/contradictory order state (missing items, deleted items, or coupon overuse); this will start breaking correctness under tens to low hundreds of concurrent checkouts.  
Fix: Wrap coupon validation+decrement and the whole order upsert/item updates in a single prisma.$transaction or convert to atomic DB operations (e.g., decrement WHERE quantity>0 and check affected rows).

[DB-2] Serverless Prisma instantiation + no pooler → connection exhaustion
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L20)
Evidence: PrismaClient is created but the singleton is only persisted in non-production; in production the client is created without a persistent global and there are no signs of a DB pooler (pgbouncer/Data Proxy) or pool settings (DATABASE_URL only).  
Impact: On serverless (Vercel/ephemeral) cold starts + many concurrent workers will create many DB connections and exhaust Postgres (typical failure around 50–200 concurrent requests depending on DB max_connections), causing outages.  
Fix: Use a production-safe singleton (persist prisma on globalThis in all environments) and deploy a connection pooler (pgbouncer/Prisma Data Proxy/Neon serverless pooling) or reconfigure to limit connections.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Unbounded product listing (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: prisma.product.findMany(...) returns all products and eagerly includes colors, with no take/limit/cursor pagination.  
Impact: As product table grows, this will cause large result sets, high memory and latency on each request and break the listing endpoint under moderate concurrent read load (~500+ concurrent users).  
Fix: Add pagination (cursor/take/skip), only select required fields, and lazy-load heavy relations like colors.

[DB-5] Category filter/ordering uses full scans (no index + no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/category/[category]/route.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: findMany(where: { category, isActive, price/stock filters }, orderBy createdAt) is executed without limits, and the schema provides no index on Product.category, isActive, or createdAt.  
Impact: Filters and ORDER BY will cause sequential scans on large product tables, producing slow queries and timeouts as rows grow past ~100k.  
Fix: Add indexes for category+isActive (composite when used together) and on createdAt (or use a covering index for the common ORDER BY), and enforce pagination.

--- INFO ---

[DB-6] Payment confirmation correctly uses a DB transaction
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (L1-L150)
Evidence: verify-payment wraps order.update and per-item stock decrements in a prisma.$transaction block, ensuring atomic status change and stock adjustments.
